**板块**｜网络安全及云端板块领涨全场，三线齐飞： CRWD 急升8.25%、 NET 涨7.29%、 PANW 升7.22%，数据平台股 SNOW 亦造好3.65%。能源股逆市靠稳，在油气双雄带动下反复向上， CVX 升2.88%、 XOM 升2.79%，成为防守资金的去向。半导体板块则严重分化， SMTC 升5.50%、通讯设备股 NOK 升3.30%，但AI互联及存储一线重挫， CRDO 暴跌9.51%、 WDC 挫2.97%。消费及零售股普遍受压， TGT 急泻3.38%、 LOW 跌2.78%，汽车股 F 跌2.85%；出行股 UBER 挫3.43%，软件股 ADBE 跌2.49%，医药重磅股 LLY 跌2.54%，加密相关股 COIN 跌2.74%。新兴市场金融股 NU 逆市升2.92%。

**焦点**｜全日最大单一跌幅来自燃料电池股 BE ，大泻11.24%，主因为前一交易日盘后公布的业绩；存储股 WDC 同样于前一交易日盘后交卷，今日收跌2.97%，两者的波动均为财报后的直接反应。至于跌幅榜第二位的 CRDO ，并非财报日,其9.51%的急泻与同属半导体链的 SMTC 升5.50%形成尖锐对照，反映资金并非整体撤离AI硬件,而是在链条内部高度拣择、强弱互换。另一值得注意的是网安三股同日录得逾7%的齐升——在61只下跌的淡市中,这类集体性的板块级跳升,通常意味着板块资金配置的切换,而非个股消息驱动。

**小结**｜全日格局是典型的「指数平稳、内部分化」：纳指近乎平收,道指却跌逾1.2%,旧经济权重与科网龙头的裂口再度扩阔,而市宽（45升61跌）更接近市场的真实温度。分析指,标普失守760关后,此位将由支持转为阻力,而纳指能否守住700关,仍是短线强弱的关键位;若权重科网的升势无法扩散至市宽,目前由少数板块撑起的指数结构将难以持久。与此同时,AI产业链的财富分配问题亦值得留意——本轮周期中最具爆发力的资产大多留在一级市场,公开市场投资者所能拣择的,只剩链条中强弱悬殊的二线标的,这或正是今日 SMTC 与 CRDO 分道扬镳的更深层背景。

AI落地卡在哪儿，大家一般都盯着模型。我现在觉得保险这一块的分量可能更重。去年几家美国大保险公司就陆续在向监管申请了，要把AI相关的损失从企业责任险里排除掉。他们给的理由其实挺实在：模型出错不是一家一家地出，一个版本上线，所有客户同一天出事，这种相关性精算根本定不了价。

排除条款一加，风险就原地转给客户了。你公司上了个agent，它自己发出错报价、错单、错诊断，赔的钱全在你自己资产负债表上，保单不管。上不上agent这件事，也就从技术部门内部的讨论，变成了要CFO和法务签字的事。

pilot为什么永远转不了production，常见的解释是模型还不够好。我觉得没那么玄，更可能就是没人敢签那个字。你要是CFO，这东西能省20%的人力，但真出事一分钱赔不回来、全记在你任内——你签吗

At other labs, for example, each team has its own KPIs, leaving little room for compromise.

Even if an infrastructure engineer proposes compressing the KV cache further, they’ll inevitably face pushback from the algorithm team if it hurts model performance.

But the most interesting point in the piece goes a step further: even if the algorithm team agrees to experiment with a new architecture that enables greater KV cache compression, the experiment may fail to produce a leading model.

We saw this with V4. When DeepSeek V4 Pro came out and lagged behind GLM 5.3 and Kimi K3, everyone started saying DeepSeek was past its prime.

TSMC is finally set to resume SRAM scaling with its A14 node, following a stall that began after N5, according to Korean media reports.

SRAM bitcell sizes have remained at 0.021 µm² for roughly eight years since the introduction of the N5 (5 nm) process in 2020. With A14, however, the size of a high-density 6T SRAM (static random-access memory) bitcell is expected to shrink to below 0.017 µm².

Korean media noted that this would put TSMC ahead of Intel’s 18A process, for which Intel reported a high-density bitcell size of 0.021 µm² and a maximum SRAM macro density of 38.1 megabits/mm² at last year’s ISSCC.

SRAM is the ultrafast cache memory used inside CPUs, GPUs, and AI accelerators. Smaller bitcells—the smallest individual memory cells—allow more memory to fit into the same area, directly affecting performance and power efficiency.

This chart is an oversimplification, but it’s the core of why I’m not selling, even at these levels.

Since January 2025, the SOX is up about 114%. Forward earnings for the same index are up roughly 198%. 

Earnings nearly tripled while prices only doubled, so semis are cheaper today on forward earnings than they were at the start of 2025.

So what changed in the last 20 days? The cost of the buildout went up. 

Oil above $100, inflation back at 3.7%, a 10-year above 5% and junk spreads blowing out on the most leveraged builders all make every data center more expensive to finance. Meanwhile the demand signals haven’t cracked, and GPU rental prices just hit a record.

 The war keeps oil high, oil keeps inflation sticky, sticky inflation keeps rates up, and high rates compress what the market will pay for growth. 

End the war, and that whole chain runs in reverse.

That’s the difference between this artificial problem and a real demand problem. 

You can’t negotiate demand back into existence, but you can negotiate an end to a war. This shock has an off switch, and it sits with Washington and Tehran. I can’t predict what Trump will do, but I know he’s pro-AI and pro-data center buildout.

So when semis keep getting cheaper for reasons that have nothing to do with demand, what do you do? Panic?

I’m not scared. If anything, lower prices mean a higher reward once we have a clear picture of where the risk sits.

I won’t deploy the little remaining cash until I see a clear reversal, purely for my own psychological safety, but when that reversal comes, I’ll deploy all of it

Trump made about $1.4 billion from crypto in 2025, plus more than $200 million from real estate, leaving him facing a projected tax bill of over $500 million, per Forbes calculations.

In December 2025, his company donated the development rights to his golf club in Jupiter, Florida, to a land trust, arguing the course was a natural habitat worth protecting. He kept owning and running the club.

Forbes estimates the write-off could reach around $825 million.

It’s a strategy Trump has used at least five times since 2005:

Bedminster, NJ (2005): Claimed a $39 million deduction on a property he bought for $8 million. The IRS initially valued the write-off at zero before the two sides settled.
Doral, FL: Claimed a deduction of up to $323 million, more than twice what he paid for the entire resort.
New York and California (2014–2015): The New York attorney general alleged the Trump Organization misled appraisers to inflate both donations.

A month after the Jupiter deal, Trump sued the IRS over the leak of his tax information. His own Justice Department’s settlement bars claims against him over matters that are pending or “could be pending.” Forbes argues that language could cover his 2025 taxes; Attorney General Todd Blanche told Congress it doesn’t.

A federal judge ruled in July that the lawsuit was brought to manipulate the judicial process. Trump is appealing.

Among the homeowners whose properties back onto the Jupiter fairways: Eric Trump, and IRS CEO Frank Bisignano, who took the job as the deal was being put together.
